item.description:
Tags grow into a vocabulary the shelf owns. An agent tags an artifact from the command line in one call, each tag can carry a meaning that travels with the shelf, a tag is edited from inside its collection, the Tags tab shows what is still untagged, and a shelf can require a tag of everything the command line adds.
### What's new
- From the command line, `sediment add` takes `--description` and `--tag`, so an agent files a tagged artifact in one call; `sediment update --tag` and `--untag` add or remove a tag without rewriting the description, and the reply says which tags are new to the shelf (SED-97). - `sediment tags` prints every tag in use with its count, and `sediment find --untagged` lists the artifacts carrying none (SED-97). - Each tag can carry a one-line meaning, kept in the shelf folder and shared with every Mac. `sediment tags describe` writes one and `sediment tags` shows them; the Tags tab shows each meaning under its tag, says *No meaning yet* where there is none, and tints a tag only one artifact carries; Go to…'s `#` reaches a described tag even when nothing carries it (SED-97). - Inside a tag's collection, Edit Tag… (⌥⌘T) gives the tag a meaning, renames it on every artifact, merges it into another tag, or removes it from all of them, each in one step with one ⌘Z, which the toast names; a merge and a removal ask first, and a rename to a name already in use points you at Merge into…. A collection nothing carries says how to leave it or edit its tag (SED-97). - The Suggestions tab lists the artifact you’re reading above the ones like it, marked when a walk brings you back to it with K; you can turn this off in Settings ▸ General ▸ Artifacts. - The Tags tab's first row, Untagged, opens the artifacts carrying no tag, so the ones `sediment find --untagged` lists are one click away (SED-108). - Settings ▸ General ▸ This shelf can require a tag from the command line: with it on, an agent’s `sediment add` or `update` that would leave an artifact untagged is refused and told to pass `--tag`. The setting travels with the shelf, and `sediment shelf` reports it (SED-109).
### Changed
- A tag an agent introduces from the command line is a line in Activity. - Show and hide the sidebar with ⌘B. ⌃⌘S no longer does anything.
### Fixed
- Closing Info during a Suggestions walk leaves the keyboard on the page, so the arrows keep scrolling it instead of moving the sidebar and ending the walk. - In Settings ▸ Appearance, VoiceOver now names the theme you are on as you move through the thumbnails with ⇥ or the arrow keys, where before it named Flint whichever theme was chosen.

Settings splits into three tabs, General, Appearance and Shelf folder, each shown whole without scrolling, in place of one long scrolling page, and Sediment has six themes, each shown as a small picture of the shelf window in its colours.
### What's new
- Settings opens on General every time, with Open at login, the artifact settings and the command line tool. Appearance holds the mode, the theme, the menu bar icon and the type faces; Shelf folder holds where your shelf lives (SED-98). - Adapt artifacts to mode moves to General, beside Default zoom, because it changes how artifacts look rather than Sediment's own windows. - The type faces sit under a live example: a title, a description and a line of small print, each redrawn the moment you pick a face. - The menu bar icon offers pages, a tray and a folder, drawn larger in Settings. A choice you already made carries over. - Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Theme offers six themes: Strata, Lichen, Verdigris, Shale, Graphite and Flint, warm to cool, then black and white with no colour at all. Each is drawn as a miniature shelf window — the sidebar, toolbar and ribbon in its colours, the artifact white as it always is — in light or dark, whichever Mode is showing. A click applies it to every window at once; Tab reaches the row, and the Left and Right arrows move through it.
### Changed
- Strata is the theme for anyone who hasn't chosen one. - Moss is retired; if you were using it, Sediment now shows Strata.
### Fixed
- A Suggestions walk keeps the keyboard on the page, as History's diff does: ↩ in, J and K through the suggestions, and the arrows scroll the page you landed on instead of moving the sidebar and ending the walk.

The right panel is complete: History keeps every version of an artifact and shows what changed, Devices moves out of Settings with Forget… for a Mac you no longer use, and Suggestions lists the artifacts most like the one you're reading. A shelf on this Mac can move into iCloud Drive at any time.
### What's new
- The right panel gains History, on ⌥⌘3: every version of an artifact's content Sediment has seen, newest first under the day it was kept, with Current and Read marked. A click on a version shows what changed since the one before it, paragraph by paragraph, in place of the page. Return from the list opens the newest version's changes, J and K walk to older and newer versions, and Escape brings the page back. Versions live in the shelf folder and are thinned as they age, so a shelf shared between Macs shows the same history on each. It takes the place of the Highlights placeholder. - The right panel gains Devices, on ⌥⌘1: every device that opens your shelf, grouped as Not caught up, Up to date and Retired, each saying when it last opened the shelf and how many deletions wait on it. Retire and Restore sit beside each device, as they did in Settings, and a device with nothing waiting can be retired too. It takes the place of the Comments placeholder, and Settings no longer has a Macs section. - Activity's line about a device that hasn't opened the shelf in a while now says to retire it under Devices (⌥⌘1). - A retired device can be forgotten 30 days after it last opened the shelf: Forget… asks first, then takes it off the list on every Mac. If it opens the shelf again, it rejoins as a new device. - The right panel gains Suggestions, on ⌥⌘4: up to eight artifacts whose names and tags most resemble the selected one, best first, each with the date it last changed and the tags it shares. A click opens that artifact, and Back (⌘[) returns. Archived artifacts are included and the Trash is not. It takes the place of the Links placeholder, and the panel's tabs now read Devices, Tags, History, Suggestions, on ⌥⌘1 to ⌥⌘4 in that order, so Tags moves to ⌥⌘2. - Return from the list walks the suggestions: it opens the first, J and K step through the list as it stood when you pressed Return, and Escape goes back to the artifact you started from. - Settings ▸ Shelf folder shows where your shelf lives — iCloud Drive, the built-in folder or a folder you choose — with a way to each. Keep in iCloud Drive…, also in the File menu, copies your shelf into the Sediment folder in iCloud Drive and leaves the folder it was in unchanged. If that folder already holds a shelf, Sediment shows that one instead and adds nothing to it.
### Fixed
- A copy iCloud Drive makes of a file whose contents match the artifact already on the shelf is set aside instead of appearing as a second artifact. - A notice about many files names three of them and counts the rest, instead of listing every one. - The launch banner's line about files still arriving goes away once a pass finds nothing left to wait for.
